summary: Claude loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, treated the "add logging" brief as architectural, ran a long multi-question design dialogue, wrote a 218-line spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-logging-subsystem-design.md, presented it for review with no implementation code written, and only after "looks good, go ahead" moved on to hyperpowers:writing-plans.
reasoning: Every acceptance criterion was satisfied and verified against both the screen and the on-disk artifacts/session log: brainstorming skill loaded first, architectural path taken explicitly, spec file written and surfaced for approval with no code written, and no bounded/spike shortcut. Notable but non-blocking issues: the Codex review gate returned empty results (stub build) and the spec is gitignored.

observations.description: Codex review gates produced nothing: agent reported "The Codex spec gate produced nothing. Preflight returned ok ... but the companion returned an empty result for each, same as the approach gate. That's a 0.0.0-stub build". The story says a Codex stub IS seeded as installed, so the gate silently degrades rather than reviewing — agent recorded it in an "ungated ledger (20260917T022018Z-52575-28487)".

The agent created a new .gitignore containing `docs/superpowers` and `docs/hyperpowers`, so the spec document it just wrote is deliberately untracked by git (git status shows only `?? .gitignore`). If a criterion expects a committed spec artifact, this ignores it.
Launch flow required clicking through four onboarding dialogs (theme picker, security notes, folder trust, bypass-permissions warning) despite HOWTO claiming dialog-bypass state was seeded.

Very long brainstorming interrogation: 7 separate AskUserQuestion prompts / multi-tab forms (scope, sink, redaction, usernames, tooling, approach, userRef, part 1, part 2) before the spec. Each question is a wall of prose; a human partner with a one-line request may find this heavy, though it did surface real tradeoffs.
Spec production took ~7 minutes wall clock ("Baked for 7m 2s") with the screen mostly frozen during gate runs.

criteria.evidence: Session log tool_use dump (jq over ~/.claude/projects/.../*.jsonl) shows first tool call: "Skill: hyperpowers:brainstorming", followed by repo Reads and AskUserQuestion calls, before any Write.

criteria.criterion: Classified ARCHITECTURAL; spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-logging-subsystem-design.md" and later "Per the architectural path, the next step is the writing-plans skill." On disk: `wc -l docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-16-logging-subsystem-design.md` → 218 lines, header "# Logging Subsystem Design ... Status: approved for planning".

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before any implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Please review the spec and tell me if you want changes. Once you approve it, the next step is the writing-plans skill ... no code until then." `git status --short` at approval time showed only `?? .gitignore` — app.js/src untouched, no logger source files.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded / skip spec
criteria.evidence: No in-chat-only design; a spec file exists at docs/hyperpowers/specs/ and the agent named the "architectural path" and "spec review gate" on screen.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / probe plan
criteria.evidence: No probe or throwaway-experiment language on screen; the flow went design questions → approach gate → spec doc → writing-plans skill ("Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill").
